question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-1]\times [1,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{5}-y+10 \\ xy-{y}^{2}+3\end{aligned}]. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[-1,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration, rounding your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
$[$ $5$ $-1$ $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-8$ $]$
{{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
${x}_{1}≈[$ {{field-4}} $]$
$0.786$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{5}-y+10) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{5}-y+10) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-{y}^{2}+3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-{y}^{2}+3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{x}^{4} & -1 \\ y & x-2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}5{x}^{4} & -1 \\ y & x-2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{5}-y+10 \\ xy-{y}^{2}+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}5{x}^{4} & -1 \\ y & x-2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{5}-y+10 \\ xy-{y}^{2}+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}5(-1)^{4} & -1 \\ 1 & (-1)-2(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(-1)^{5}-(1)+10 \\ (-1)(1)-{1}^{2}+3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{14} \\ -\frac{3}{14}\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{14} \\ -\frac{3}{14}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{14} \\ -\frac{3}{14}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{37}{14} \\ \frac{11}{14}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-2.643 \\ 0.786\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
